args.question: What threshold or criteria should be used to identify maintenance records with "poor cost efficiency"? Should I delete records where MCE (MaintenanceCostUSD + CleaningCostUSD + ReplacementCostUSD) / GenCapMW exceeds a specific value, or should I delete the top X% of records with highest MCE? What is the exact cutoff?

result: The prompt specifies that "poor cost efficiency" is defined as when the Maintenance Cost Efficiency (MCE) exceeds 290. The MCE is calculated as the sum of maintenance, cleaning, and replacement costs divided by the plant's generation capacity in megawatts (GenCapMW).

content: What threshold or criteria should be used to identify maintenance records with "poor cost efficiency"? Should I delete records where MCE (MaintenanceCostUSD + CleaningCostUSD + ReplacementCostUSD) / GenCapMW exceeds a specific value, or should I delete the top X% of records with highest MCE? What is the exact cutoff?

args.sql:
SELECT m.maintregistry, m.maintcostusd, m.cleancostusd, m.replacecostusd, p.gencapmw, 
       ROUND(CAST((m.maintcostusd + m.cleancostusd + m.replacecostusd) AS numeric) / p.gencapmw, 2) as mce
FROM maintenance m
JOIN plant p ON m.powerref = p.growregistry
LIMIT 10;

DELETE FROM maintenance
WHERE maintregistry IN (
    SELECT m.maintregistry
    FROM maintenance m
    JOIN plant p ON m.powerref = p.growregistry
    WHERE (m.maintcostusd + m.cleancostusd + m.replacecostusd) / p.gencapmw > 290
);
